exposure: Meconium-stained amniotic fluid (MSAF) in deliveries complicated by maternal intrapartum fever (IF)
Clear amniotic fluid (CAF) in deliveries complicated by maternal intrapartum fever (IF)
outcome: CD due to non-reassuring fetal heart rate
Placental cultures yielding extended spectrum beta-lactamase pathogens
Placental cultures yielding Group B Streptococcus
cohort: The study included all singleton pregnancies from 2014 to 2020 that experienced maternal intrapartum fever >= 38 degC during a trial of labor.
finding: Women experiencing intrapartum fever and meconium-stained amniotic fluid during labor have an elevated risk of cesarean delivery and positive placental cultures, particularly with gastrointestinal and extended spectrum beta-lactamase pathogens, compared to those with intrapartum fever alone.
mod_finding: The MSAF&IF group exhibited significantly higher rates of cesarean delivery (p = 0.001) and cesarean delivery due to non-reassuring fetal heart rate (p = 0.001).
